title: Plainsmen open conference season with sweep over South | Cheyenne South | wyomingnews.com
text:
CHEYENNE — Over the past few seasons, Cheyenne South’s volleyball team has garnered a reputation for being a scrappy team capable of punishing a team’s mistakes.
That came to a head when the Bison faced off against Laramie, as South managed to keep all three sets close for long portions of its contest with the Plainsmen.
However, the Plainsmen’s high-end hitting proved to be too much for the Bison. Laramie pulled away in each set to pick up a 25-13, 25-14, 25-16 win over South to kick off the Class 4A East Conference portion of the 2025 season.
“I liked the energy that we brought,” Plainsmen coach Erin Wedemeyer said. “We’ve struggled a little bit on and off with some of our tournaments, but they had good energy throughout all three sets.”
Senior Tessa Dodd led the Plainsmen with 15 kills. She also added 12 digs, a serving ace and an assist. Classmate Ava Plassmeyer recorded a team-high five aces to go along with six kills and six digs. Kierra Gardner notched a team-high 17 assists.
“South is a great team that’s really competitive and scrappy,” Dodd said. “We were just focused on play-by-play and focusing on what we could control.”
While South wasn’t able to keep the set close forever, it still did a good job of hanging with the Plainsmen through the first half of each set. It’s something positive Bison coach Kiarra Fulk said her team can build on moving forward.
“It was a good start to our conference season for us to see what we need to work on,” the coach said. “Seeing some fast arm swings from Laramie was great because they are a really good, strong team and are especially their tall blocks.
“We really worked on aiming tall, aiming for hand and working around them. I thought my girls were doing a better job of that throughout the sets.”
The first two sets played out nearly identically. South and Laramie went back and forth, with the Plainsmen unable to push their advantage to more than a few points. After taking a 6-4 lead early in the first frame, Laramie rattled off a 6-0 run to take a 12-4 lead.
South then won six of the next nine points to cut the lead back to five, but was unable to come any closer. The Bison were outscored 10-3 from that point to drop the first set.
After falling behind 2-0 to open the second frame, South rattled off three consecutive points to take its first lead of the match. Laramie eventually jumped out to a 10-6 lead before Fulk called a timeout. The Bison won three straight points to cut the lead back to one.
But, like the first set, Laramie responded with a run of its own, with back-to-back four-point runs to take a 19-11 lead. In the end, the Plainsmen outscored South 14-2 to close out the frame.
“We just tried to focus on what we could control,” Dodd said. “As a team, we all focused on being one, and that was really great.”
Laramie had its fastest start of the day in the third set, ripping off five consecutive points to open the final frame. South managed to cut the lead to four on three separate occasions throughout the set, but was unable to come any closer. In the end, a hitting error on match point gave the Plainsmen the set and match win.
It wasn’t the cleanest match Laramie has ever played according to both Dodd and Wedemeyer, but it was, all-in-all, a great start to the year. But with a long way to go, the Plainsmen know their best days are ahead of them.
“I want to see continued energy, regardless of what’s happening with the score,” Wedemeyer said. “Being able to keep that intensity and energy during first ball kills and those kinds of things (will be what helps us moving forward).”
For the Bison, the match wasn’t as lopsided as the final score indicated. While the errors the Bison made ultimately cost them, Fulk wasn’t displeased with all of them.
Fulk was also pleased with liberos Lyric Gay and Allyson Felix-Santos, who had excellent matches for the Bison.
“As I told my girls, we’re down to make aggressive errors,” Fulk said. “We were making what I call positive errors. So cleaning up our positive errors and making them more aggressive and in the court, that will truly help us because our serve receive is going to be strong.”
Top-ranked Laramie will head to Gillette Saturday to face No. 3-ranked Thunder Basin at noon Saturday. South will head to Rapid City, South Dakota, for the Rapid City Invitational, which kicks off Friday.
